## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uddesavāra* ("Specification Section" or "Indication Section") is the second textual division of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 2, PTS pp. 1–3), situated as the first subsection of the explanatory division (*vibhāga*) directly following the opening *Saṅgahavāra* [von Hinüber 1996; Caudron 2000]. Functioning as an initial outline and brief commentary on the introductory verses, it sets forth the foundational categories of the *Netti*'s exegetical method [von Hinüber 1996; Caudron 2000]. It provides the formal enumeration of the sixteen interpretive modes (*hāra*), the five guidelines or methods (*naya*), and the eighteen root-terms or constituents (*mūlapada*) [Balasooriya et al. 1980; Caudron 2000; von Hinüber 1996]. These foundational categories define the structural framework of the treatise, which receives detailed exegesis in subsequent divisions such as the *Hāravibhaṅga*, *Hārasampāta*, and *Nayasamuṭṭhāna* [Balasooriya et al. 1980].

- [Caudron 2000] Marian Winston Caudron, Guide to Skillful Means: Reexamining the Netti-Pakaraṇa's Modes and Methods (2000) — Role of the Uddesa-vāra in sketching the sixteen hāras, five nayas, and eighteen mūlapadas, as well as English translation variants.
